title: RAPHAEL - feasibility study for the integration of palliative care in severe heart failure
summary: This is a substudy of an  Europe-wide, multicenter, single-arm, exploratory qualitative feasibility study. Multicenter means that the project is not only taking place at Aachen University Hospital, but in several European countries. Single-arm means that there is one group of patients being studied in the project, namely people with heart failure. An exploratory study is a project conducted as a comprehensive survey to test the effectiveness of the research method with a view to a larger study. A feasibility study examines how well the application works and gathers suggestions for improving the app. Starting in May 2026, a total of five patients, five family members, and two healthcare professionals will be included in the project. The project will last a total of four weeks. During this time, patients will enter their symptoms into the PAL@HEART app and will then be interviewed once. In the RAPHAEL project, we aim to improve care for people with heart failure. To this end, we are interested in experiences with the PAL@HEART app. An important component is the RAPHAEL questionnaire in the PAL@HEART app regarding symptoms and needs. This is a short online questionnaire that assesses the severity of symptoms—both physical and psychological—as well as social symptoms and questions regarding meaning and purpose in life. The questionnaire should be completd at least once, but ideally every day for a period of four weeks. This will be followed by an interview lasting about 30 minutes. During this conversation, we will speak with patients and their family members about their experiences with the PAL@HEART app. We want to understand how the app has worked, what is important in daily life with heart failure, what works well, and in which areas patients and family members would like more support, as well as how healthcare professionals can use the app.

interventions.name: Feasibility study on the PAL@heart app, including assessment of symptom severity in heart failure using a questionnaire (based on the USD4D questionnaire and results from previous phases of the RAPHAEL project), along with semi-structured interviews following the 4-week application phase. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent
Individuals who are legally competent and mentally capable of following the researchers’ instructions, completing questionnaires, and participating in an interview
Presence of heart failure (all stages) in patients only
Exclusion criteria:
Persons who are institutionalized pursuant to an order from a government agency or a court
Persons who are in a relationship of dependency or employment with the examiner
